completion_conditions: A plan task entry declaring a runtime under either key registers a task carrying that value; the claude-code default applies only when neither key is present.
A plan task entry declaring a runtime that is not task-capable, or declaring both keys with different values, is refused by name at ingest and at registration - before any mirror write.
mergegate_check._frozen_task_match_errors reports a runtime mismatch regardless of which key the frozen plan used, and never raises out of the gate.

.shiki/schemas/plan.schema.json and cmd_plan_guide each name the key, and set-equality binders pin the plan-schema enum to the task-schema enum and the two registration paths' record key sets to each other.
The existing mirror is unchanged and still valid: no plan file is edited, validate_shiki --target . passes, and the mirror schema-conformance loop reports no new failure.

decisions: THE DEFECT, MEASURED. register_task_from_plan (scripts/shiki_tasks.py:340) reads `task_plan.get("runtime", "claude-code")`. Reproduced 2026-08-24 against the real modules: a plan task entry declaring `assigned_runtime: "codex"` registers a task with `assigned_runtime: "claude-code"`, and that task then PASSES shiki_runtime.validate_task_runtime_for_execution - so a plan meaning codex dispatches to Claude Code with no error anywhere. The same entry declaring `runtime: "codex"` registers `codex` correctly.

THE SECOND FACE: THE GATE IS BLIND TOO. mergegate_check._frozen_task_match_errors compares runtime only when `frozen.get("runtime")` is truthy. Measured against the same task: frozen `{"assigned_runtime": "codex"}` vs a `claude-code` task yields 0 errors; frozen `{"runtime": "codex"}` vs the same task yields 1. So an alias-declared runtime bypasses the frozen-plan binding entirely, and plan.schema.json accepts the alias silently (additionalProperties: true).

CORPUS, AUDITED. 79 plan task entries across 33 mirror plans: 73 declare `runtime` (60 claude-code, 13 codex), 5 declare neither, and exactly ONE declares `assigned_runtime` (P-20260822T100256491531Z-04bae792, value "claude"). So `runtime` is unambiguously the canonical plan-side key - the wrong key is a one-off authoring slip, not a systemic pattern. It is also what the handoff surface emits (shiki_tasks.py:590, :1210, :1235; shiki_runtime.py:395), which is why the plan-side and record-side names differ in the first place; the comment at mergegate_check.py:394 documents the mismatch as intentional.

DECISION - ALIAS, PREFERRING `runtime` (operator, 2026-08-24). Carry `runtime`; fall back to `assigned_runtime`; hard error when both are present and disagree. ONE shared resolver, used by registration AND the frozen-plan gate, so the alias binds in a single place. Rejected: strict `runtime`-only with a loud ingest error (collapses to one name and lets the schema enumerate freely, but refuses rather than honours a pure naming slip and cannot help a plan already frozen); and renaming the plan-side key to `assigned_runtime` (ends the representation mismatch but contradicts 73 of 79 entries and the handoff surface).

DECISION - REJECT AN UNKNOWN VALUE AT REGISTRATION AND AT INGEST (operator, 2026-08-24). Today an invalid runtime flows through registration and only surfaces at validate_shiki or at dispatch. It becomes a named error at require_grilled_plan (ingest) and at register_task_from_plan, against the runtime registry's task-capable names. Because register_task_from_plan appends its ledger entry BEFORE writing the task file, the refusal must raise before the ledger append or a refused registration leaves an orphan ledger entry.

THE RETROACTIVITY TRAP, MEASURED - AND WHY validate_plan IS ASYMMETRIC. P-20260822T100256491531Z-04bae792 is spec-frozen, its goal G-20260822T100310254979Z-b0f195ee is complete, and it declares `assigned_runtime: "claude"` - a value that is not in the runtime registry at all. It can never be edited. Measured across all 33 mirror plans: a `runtime`-value check breaks 0; a both-keys-present-and-different check breaks 0 (no plan declares both); an `assigned_runtime`-VALUE check breaks exactly that one. Likewise for the schema: declaring `runtime` with an enum breaks 0 plans, declaring `assigned_runtime` as {"type":"string"} breaks 0, and enumerating `assigned_runtime` fails that plan immediately. So validate_plan and plan.schema.json validate the canonical key's value and the key conflict, but NOT the alias's value - deliberately, with the reason recorded at the check. The strict both-key check lives at require_grilled_plan instead, which only ever sees plans being ingested. This is the same trap the sibling cca_checklist_profile slice hit.

DECISION - SCHEMA AND GUIDE BOTH NAME THE KEY (operator, 2026-08-24). plan.schema.json declares `runtime` with an enum set-equal to task.schema.json's `assigned_runtime` enum, and declares `assigned_runtime` as a described string alias. cmd_plan_guide (scripts/shiki_tasks.py:817) gains an `optional_task_fields` block naming every field registration actually carries - its silence, documenting only title/scope/acceptance_checks, is the documented reason the wrong key was written. cca_checklist_profile is deliberately NOT named: registration still drops it, so naming it would be a lie (that is the sibling slice, kept out of this one by the operator's 2026-08-22 decision).

DECISION - _FROZEN_TASK_MATCH_FIELDS IS NOT RESTRUCTURED. Its loop compares task[field] to frozen[field] under identical names; the runtime check below it is bespoke precisely because the names differ, and the constant's own comment says so. Routing that bespoke check through the shared resolver is the whole fix. Turning the constant into a name mapping would be churn on a governance-critical surface for no added coverage.

DECISION - SCOPE EDGE (operator, 2026-08-24). IN: the two-path key-set binder in tests/test_paired_invariants.py, because register_task_from_plan and cmd_issue_plan emit byte-identical key sets today and nothing asserts it - set-equality is the check that catches the next one-path-only field. OUT, as explicit non-goals: scripts/shiki_cli.py:355's hardcoded --runtime choices (missing `codex-front`, which 9 live tasks use) and the `github-actions` entry in task.schema.json's assigned_runtime enum that no registry role permits on a task. Three runtime vocabularies disagree today (registry task-capable = 6 names, task schema enum = 7, CLI choices = 6-but-different); reconciling them is a separate goal with its own risk assessment.

DECISION - NO SADR (operator, 2026-08-24). The alias is a naming decision, not an architecture one, and the resolver docstring, the schema description and the plan guide record it on the three surfaces a planner actually reads. Adding a SADR would bump the exact-set range(1,N) pin in tests/test_adr_references.py and pull docs/adr/README.md into the locks for no durable gain.

RISK - HIGH (operator, 2026-08-24). Measured precedent: every registered task whose locks include scripts/mergegate_check.py or scripts/shiki_contracts.py and that changes what MergeGate blocks is classified high or critical; none are low or medium. The change here strictly WIDENS what the gate catches and weakens no existing block, but it is still a gate binding plus the shared-contracts module, so it takes the Guardian gate.

LOCKS AND CONFLICTS, MEASURED. .shiki/locks holds 0 records in state `active`, and shiki_locks.active_lock_conflicts returns NONE for the full candidate set (shiki_contracts.py, shiki_tasks.py, validate_shiki.py, mergegate_check.py, plan.schema.json, tests/test_plan_runtime_key.py, tests/test_paired_invariants.py). scripts/test_shiki_module_boundaries.sh imposes no import-direction rule, only importability, and shiki_contracts is a leaf (json, pathlib, shiki_runtime_registry) already imported by both mergegate_check and validate_shiki - so it is the correct home for a resolver all three call sites share.

CONTEXT & IMPACT EVIDENCE - CI-08 DEVIATION, RECORDED. AGENTS.md CI-08 asks that Context & Impact for a non-trivial Goal be produced by a Workflow parallel exploration sweep. The operator explicitly accepted an inline sweep instead on 2026-08-24: the findings above were produced by direct measurement against the real scripts/ modules (a scratchpad harness importing shiki_tasks, mergegate_check, shiki_runtime, shiki_schema and shiki_locks) rather than by a multi-agent fan-out. Every claim in this plan is a measured result, not an assertion.

Operator-reported defect, re-measured in-worktree against the real scripts/ modules; six design decisions settled by the operator through two grill rounds (key policy, value-check placement, plan-schema shape, plan-guide scope, scope edge, risk, decision record). outcome: A plan task entry's declared runtime reaches the registered task's assigned_runtime through one shared resolver that accepts `runtime` (canonical) and `assigned_runtime` (alias); a runtime that is not task-capable is a named refusal at plan ingest and at registration instead of a silent default; plan.schema.json and `shiki plan guide` both name the key and its accepted values; and the frozen-plan gate binds through the same resolver, so an alias-declared runtime can no longer bypass the binding.

spec_freeze.source: Operator approved the drafted requirements in the Claude Code planning session on 2026-08-24, answering the Spec Freeze confirmation with 'Approve - freeze it' after reviewing the reproduced defect (a plan entry declaring assigned_runtime: codex registers claude-code and passes validate_task_runtime_for_execution), the blind frozen-plan gate (0 errors for the alias form vs 1 for runtime), the 79-entry corpus audit across 33 mirror plans, the six settled design decisions (alias preferring runtime with one shared resolver; rejection at ingest and at registration; the plan-schema and plan-guide wording; the key-set binder in and the CLI/enum vocabulary fixes out; no SADR), the measured validate_plan and plan.schema.json asymmetry forced by the un-editable spec-frozen plan P-20260822T100256491531Z-04bae792, and the high risk classification. Recorded by the planner on the operator's instruction; the approval is the operator's.

acceptance_checks: scripts/shiki_contracts.py defines a single plan-task runtime resolver that returns the `runtime` value when only `runtime` is present, the `assigned_runtime` value when only `assigned_runtime` is present, that same value when both are present and EQUAL, and None when neither key is present.
That resolver raises a ValueError subclass whose message names both keys and both values when a task entry declares `runtime` and `assigned_runtime` with DIFFERENT values.

scripts/shiki_contracts.py also exposes a task-capability helper derived from shiki_runtime_registry (roles intersecting TASK_RUNTIME_ROLES), and `bash scripts/test_shiki_module_boundaries.sh` passes with shiki_tasks, validate_shiki and mergegate_check all importing from it.
register_task_from_plan with a task entry {"runtime": "codex", ...} writes assigned_runtime == "codex".
register_task_from_plan with a task entry {"assigned_runtime": "codex", ...} writes assigned_runtime == "codex". (Measured before the change: "claude-code".)
register_task_from_plan with a task entry declaring NEITHER key writes assigned_runtime == "claude-code".
register_task_from_plan with {"runtime": "claude"} and with {"assigned_runtime": "claude"} each raise ShikiError naming the value 'claude' and the accepted task-capable runtime names.
That refusal happens BEFORE any mirror write: after the raise, the target's .shiki/tasks/ and .shiki/ledger/ each contain no new file. A test asserts the directory contents, not just the exception.
The literal "runtime" no longer appears inside the body of register_task_from_plan; the resolver call is the only place a plan-entry runtime key is read.
require_grilled_plan raises ShikiError for a plan whose task entry declares a runtime that is not task-capable under EITHER key, naming the task index, the offending value and the accepted names.
require_grilled_plan raises ShikiError for a plan whose task entry declares both keys with different values.

validate_plan in scripts/validate_shiki.py raises ValidationError for a mirror plan whose task entry declares a non-task-capable value under the `runtime` key, and for one declaring both keys with different values. It does NOT validate the `assigned_runtime` value, and a comment at the check names .shiki/plans/P-20260822T100256491531Z-04bae792.json as the reason.

.shiki/schemas/plan.schema.json's task item declares `runtime` with an enum set-equal to .shiki/schemas/task.schema.json's assigned_runtime enum, and declares `assigned_runtime` as {"type": "string"} with a description marking it the accepted alias.

Every plan under .shiki/plans/ still passes the mirror schema-conformance loop after the schema change (measured today: 0 failures for exactly this shape; enumerating `assigned_runtime` instead yields 1 failure on P-20260822T100256491531Z-04bae792).

cmd_plan_guide's plan_contract gains an optional_task_fields entry naming `runtime` with its accepted values plus non_goals, dependencies, locks, risk_level, required_skills, test_command, expected_branch, expected_pr and github_issue, and does NOT name cca_checklist_profile.

mergegate_check._frozen_task_match_errors resolves the frozen plan's runtime through the shared resolver, so a frozen entry declaring `assigned_runtime: "codex"` against a claude-code task yields the same mismatch error a `runtime`-declaring entry yields today. (Measured before the change: 0 errors vs 1 error for the two forms.)
A frozen task entry declaring both keys with different values, or declaring a non-task-capable value, yields a blocking reason from _frozen_task_match_errors - never an uncaught exception.
_FROZEN_TASK_MATCH_FIELDS in scripts/mergegate_check.py is byte-unchanged.

tests/test_paired_invariants.py gains a binder asserting the plan.schema.json task-item `runtime` enum is SET-EQUAL to the task.schema.json assigned_runtime enum, in the module's existing style, with a divergence test that fails on a mutated copy and a message naming both files.

tests/test_paired_invariants.py gains a binder asserting the record key sets emitted by register_task_from_plan and cmd_issue_plan are SET-EQUAL, with a divergence test that fails on a mutated copy and a message naming both functions.

The new behavioural tests live in tests/test_plan_runtime_key.py, and each behavioural assertion is paired with a divergence assertion that feeds the old code path the same input and asserts the old wrong answer.

tasks.scope:
In scripts/shiki_contracts.py (a leaf module that imports only json, pathlib and shiki_runtime_registry, and that mergegate_check, validate_shiki and shiki_tasks can all import without a cycle), add ONE shared resolver for a plan task entry's declared runtime, plus a task-capability helper built on the runtime registry. The resolver is the single authority on which key names a plan may use: it prefers `runtime`, falls back to `assigned_runtime`, returns None when neither is present, returns the shared value when both are present and equal, and raises a ValueError subclass naming both keys and both values when both are present and differ. Its docstring records the decision and its reason: `runtime` is canonical (73 of 79 existing plan task entries use it, and the handoff surface emits `runtime` at shiki_tasks.py:590/:1210/:1235), `assigned_runtime` is the accepted alias because a planner reaching for the task record's own field name is the mistake that actually happened, and honouring a declared value beats silently defaulting.

In scripts/shiki_tasks.py, replace `task_plan.get("runtime", "claude-code")` at line 340 with a resolver call, and validate the resolved value against the runtime registry BEFORE any mirror write. register_task_from_plan currently calls append_ledger before write_json, so an unknown runtime must raise before the ledger append or a refusal leaves an orphan ledger entry behind. The `claude-code` default applies only when the resolver returns None. Extend require_grilled_plan with the same resolution and validation so `shiki plan ingest` / `shiki run` refuse a plan carrying an unknown runtime or a conflicting key pair, naming the task index, the offending value and the accepted names. Extend cmd_plan_guide's `plan_contract` with an `optional_task_fields` block naming `runtime` and its accepted values alongside the other fields registration actually carries; do NOT name cca_checklist_profile, which registration still drops (that is a separate slice).

In scripts/validate_shiki.py, extend validate_plan to reject a task entry whose `runtime` value is not task-capable and to reject a conflicting key pair. Deliberately do NOT validate the `assigned_runtime` VALUE here: validate_plan runs repo-wide over the mirror, and the spec-frozen .shiki/plans/P-20260822T100256491531Z-04bae792.json declares `assigned_runtime: "claude"` (not a registry runtime at all) on a goal that is already complete. That plan is an approval-bearing frozen artifact and must never be edited, so a mirror-wide alias-value check would turn the repository red with no legal remedy. Measured: a `runtime`-value check and a key-conflict check each break 0 of the 33 mirror plans; an `assigned_runtime`-value check breaks exactly that one. Put the reason in a comment at the check, naming that plan.

In .shiki/schemas/plan.schema.json, declare the task item's `runtime` with an enum set-equal to .shiki/schemas/task.schema.json's `assigned_runtime` enum, and declare `assigned_runtime` as {"type": "string"} with a description marking it the accepted alias. The asymmetry is deliberate and load-bearing for the same reason as above: measured, this exact shape produces 0 mirror schema-loop failures, while enumerating `assigned_runtime` produces `$.tasks[0].assigned_runtime: value 'claude' is not one of [...]` on the frozen plan.

In scripts/mergegate_check.py, route the bespoke runtime check below the _FROZEN_TASK_MATCH_FIELDS loop (lines 451-458) through the same resolver, so a frozen plan entry declaring the alias binds exactly as one declaring `runtime` does today. Leave _FROZEN_TASK_MATCH_FIELDS itself byte-unchanged: its loop compares identically-named fields and restructuring it into a name mapping is churn on a governance-critical constant. The gate must degrade to a blocking reason, never an uncaught exception, when a frozen entry declares a conflicting key pair or a non-task-capable value.

In tests/test_paired_invariants.py, add two binders in the module's existing style (each with a `*_holds` test pinning the live agreement and a `*_divergence_*` test proving the binder fails on a mutated copy, with failure messages naming BOTH sites and the fix): the plan-schema `runtime` enum set-equal to the task-schema `assigned_runtime` enum, and the record key sets emitted by register_task_from_plan and cmd_issue_plan set-equal to each other. The second is the durable guard for this defect class: the two paths emit byte-identical key sets today and nothing asserts it, so the next one-path-only field would land as silently as this one did.

In tests/test_plan_runtime_key.py (new), cover the resolver, the registration carry, the pre-ledger refusal, the ingest refusal, and the gate binding. Pair each behavioural assertion with a divergence assertion that feeds the OLD code path the same input and asserts the old wrong answer, so the suite proves it detects the regression rather than merely passing today.

REPRODUCIBILITY - what this task must reproduce and then fix, measured 2026-08-24 against the real scripts/ modules:
  register_task_from_plan({"assigned_runtime": "codex", ...}) -> task assigned_runtime == 'claude-code'   (plan value dropped)
  that task through shiki_runtime.validate_task_runtime_for_execution -> PASSES (dispatches to Claude Code, silently)
  register_task_from_plan({"runtime": "codex", ...})          -> task assigned_runtime == 'codex'         (correct)
  _frozen_task_match_errors(task=claude-code, frozen={"assigned_runtime": "codex"}) -> []                 (gate blind)
  _frozen_task_match_errors(task=claude-code, frozen={"runtime": "codex"})          -> 1 error
  shiki_schema.validate_instance(plan_with_assigned_runtime, plan.schema.json)      -> accepted (additionalProperties: true)
Baseline suite before the change: `Ran 1177 tests in 130.114s / OK`.
